prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: orthographic four-view turnaround sheet for reconstructing one game-ready timber deck with Hunyuan3D multi-view.
Create a wide 2048x1024 image containing exactly four isolated views in one horizontal row, in order FRONT, LEFT, BACK, RIGHT, without any written labels. Plain pure white background, no ground, no cast shadow.
The SAME solid rectangular platform is temporarily stood upright for asset capture. It is a 6 metre wide by 4 metre tall wooden panel, with a substantial 0.6 metre thickness, not a door. It will later be laid horizontally as a bridge deck. Front is the continuous walkable top: seven or eight very broad dark honey-brown timber planks joined flush with shallow dark seams and slightly chamfered outside corners. Two very simple dark iron end straps sit flush near the left and right edges, with a few large restrained rivets. Back is the solid connected underside with two flush broad cross-battens and matching end caps. Left and right are true narrow EDGE profiles showing the full 0.6 metre thickness. Every view uses exactly the same 4 metre vertical extent and baseline; the front and back are six metres wide, and the edge profiles are 0.6 metres wide. Keep the major silhouette almost rectangular and all pieces connected. No rails, pillars, posts, legs, holes, ropes, handles, hinge hardware, spikes, curved arches, raised obstacles, text, symbols or decorations.
Style: stylized hand-painted fantasy FPS environment, moderately detailed readable game asset, broad clean faceted planes, chunky proportions, two or three coherent large colour blocks, soft painted gradients, restrained edge wear. Dark warm timber with simple charcoal iron straps, matte finish, no photorealism, no dense wood grain, no noisy cracks. Neutral even studio illumination. The front/top must be flat and unobstructed enough to walk on. Show complete object inside each column with generous clean white spacing; no perspective, no top-down view, no three-quarter view. Use consistent front and back wood layout and consistent edge thickness. This is one repeatable solid bridge floor module, presented vertically solely for shape capture.
